text: A nested loop is simply a loop inside another loop — and it's how you work with grids and pairs.
For every single pass of the outer loop, the inner loop runs all the way through.
So three rows times three columns produces a full multiplication table, printed grid-style.
[chuckle] Nesting two lists gives you every possible combination of their items.
Each color pairs with each size, producing red-small, red-large, blue-small, blue-large.
[sniff] Here's a subtle but crucial rule about break inside nested loops.
break only exits the loop it lives in — the inner one — not the outer loop around it.
So the outer loop keeps going, and the inner loop restarts fresh each time.
[groan] Nested loops are powerful, but keep them shallow — more than two or three levels gets hard to follow fast.
